Suggs' knee buckled as he went up for a layup against the Knicks on Sunday

        The Orlando Magic continue to feel cursed by injuries, and this one to Jalen Suggs looks like it could be pretty bad. In the fourth quarter of Orlando's victory over the Knicks on Sunday, Suggs took off for a full-speed layup and his right knee appeared to give out on him as he took off for the basket. Suggs immediately collapsed to the court and was in considerable pain as he was tended to on the baseline. He was not able to leave the court on his own power. 
This is the dreaded non-contact injury. The Magic will obviously hope it's not as bad as it looked, but with the injury luck they've had, you couldn't blame them if they're expecting the worst news. After the game, Magic coach Sean Sweeney did not have an update on Suggs' status. 
On Friday, they lost Paolo Banchero to a high-ankle sprain that is expected to keep him sidelined for at least a month, possibly more (high-ankle sprains tend to carry a four-to-six-week recovery timetable). Suggs has missed 62 games over the last two years to injury, and he and Franz Wagner combined to miss 73 games last year. The trio of Banchero, Wagner, and Suggs has only managed to play 25 games together over the last two seasons, and now we're only three games into this season, and Banchero and Suggs are already down. 
The win over the Knicks was the first of the season for the Magic. They are now 1-2 on the year.

title: Jalen Williams leg injury: Top-20 NBA star stretchered off court after gruesome fall - CBS Sports
description: The Oklahoma City star suffered what appeared to be a severe broken leg, an injury that may threaten to derail th
body:
The Oklahoma City star suffered what appeared to be a severe broken leg, an injury that may threaten to derail the Thunder's championship hopes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher late in the fourth quarter of a 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers after suffering what appeared to be a severe lower leg injury. With just over a minute to play, Williams drove to the basket and tried to go up for a dunk. He was sandwiched in mid-air by Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr., which caused him to lose his balance. When he landed, his left leg got trapped underneath the weight of his entire body and the lower part of it appeared to break in the wrong direction. The Thunder training staff immediately covered his leg with towels as his teammates looked on in distress. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander pulled his own jersey up over his face as Williams' leg was placed into an air cast and he was loaded onto a stretcher. "I just feel bad for him. Nothing more than that," Gilgeous-Alexander said on the court after the win. 
Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said the team had no immediate update on Williams' status. "We're not doing great," Daigneault said. "That's tough on the guys." 
Williams gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was wheeled off the court, but there's a good chance that he is done for the season. Williams was coming off season derailed by injuriesWilliams emerged as a true star in 2025, when he made his first All-Star appearance and earned a spot on the All-NBA Third Team and the All-Defensive Second Team before helping Gilgeous-Alexander lead the Thunder to their first title since moving to Oklahoma City. Williams averaged 23.6 points in the 2025 Finals and had a playoff-career-high 40 points to lead the Thunder to a Game 5 win that gave them a 3-2 series lead over the Pacers (OKC won in seven games). 
He played through a wrist injury during the 2025 playoffs, however, and underwent surgery last summer to fix the problem, which kept him sidelined for the first 19 games of last season. Less than two months into his return, he strained his right hamstring and was sidelined for multiple weeks. He came back, played two games, then tweaked his hamstring again and missed another six weeks. Williams returned shortly before the playoffs last season, but suffered a left hamstring strain in Game 2 of the Thunder's first-round series with the Phoenix Suns. He sat out the rest of that series and missed the entire second round before coming back for the Western Conference Finals against the Spurs. After a stellar Game 1, he tweaked his left hamstring again in Game 2 and only played 10 more minutes the rest of the series. When the Thunder lost Game 7 to the Spurs, which ended their repeat quest, he was forced to watch from the bench in street clothes. 
Williams' injury a major blow to Thunder's title chancesThe Thunder made some moves around the margins this offseason -- most notably, trading Lu Dort to the Atlanta Hawks -- but brought back their entire core and hoped to make another run at the title in a top-heavy Western Conference. Vegas oddsmakers installed them as the preseason favorite to win the title, and they started the season with a convincing win over the Spurs. Sunday's win over the Clippers moved the Thunder to 3-0, and even without Dort, they have the depth to withstand Williams' absence -- at least in the regular season. They won 64 games last season largely without Williams, and should once again be at the top of the standings. But last season also showed that it will be much more difficult to get through the playoffs without Williams. Though he was off to a somewhat slow start, Williams was averaging 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and one steal to begin the season, and was second on the team in scoring behind Gilgeous-Alexander. CBS Sports ranked Williams as the 20th-best player in the NBA in the annual Top 100 player rankings. 
Williams' injury appears similar to George, HaywardWe still don't have an official diagnosis for Williams, but the injury certainly appeared to be similar to those endured by Paul George and Gordon Hayward earlier in their careers. George suffered an open tibia-fibula fracture in 2014 while playing for Team USA and missed nearly the entire 2014-15 season. He recovered to make seven more All-Star appearances and four more All-NBA Teams, and even finished third in MVP voting in 2019 with the Thunder. George remains a high-level player and poured in 38 points on opening night this season, his debut with the Celtics. Hayward, on the other hand, dislocated his left ankle and fractured his left tibia on opening night of the 2017-18 season in his debut with the Celtics. He missed the remainder of that season and was never the same player. Hayward appeared in 318 more games over six seasons before retiring at 33 years old.

description: Rookie receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and KC Concepcion are tur
body:
Rookie receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and KC Concepcion are turning explosive targets into must-roster value, while Devin Singletary offers a sneaky stash before trade deadlines and backfield shifts shake up leagues
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Julian Finney / Getty Images
            
            

    
        Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season was another wild one with overtime finishes and key Fantasy Football performances that defined the week. Before we turn the page on Week 7, it's time to reflect on key standout performances and what the Week 8 waiver-wire priorities should be. From emerging wide receivers to running backs making the most of expanded opportunities, several players have put themselves on the Fantasy radar. Waiver wire standouts of the weekOmar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets Hopefully you scooped up Cooper on your wire last week, but he remains rostered in fewer leagues than he should be. That roster percentage should be 100%. Cooper proved just as explosive in Week 7 as he was in his breakout Week 6 performance. Cooper racked up 115 yards on five receptions and turned all five of his targets into a reception. He scored a touchdown and, perhaps more importantly, the Jets designed the play around him. He was lined up in the backfield. The Jets are designing red zone touches for their rookie first-round pick and with 218 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks he has entered must-start territory. KC Concepcion, WR, BrownsIf Concepcion was dropped in your league, he's another riser. His breakout performance in Week 7 included 10 targets, 129 receiving yards and eight receptions. This is a career high in targets, receptions and yards for the rookie first-round pick. Concepcion had a 29% target share, three forced missed tackles and converted seven first downs for the Browns. He's a solution maker in this offense and he gets it done before and after the catch. He racked up 110 air yards and 82 yards after the catch in another Browns victory. Concepcion is squarely in the WR2/3 mix moving forward.Standout Fantasy performancesTony Pollard, RB, TitansThe Pollard breakout finally came just as rumors have surfaced about him potentially being traded before the NFL trade deadline. Pollard was an absolute week winner with 28 combined touches (three receptions), 129 rushing yards, 26 receiving yards, and three rushing touchdowns. 
Zay Flowers, WR, RavensHow many wide receivers would you trade Zay Flowers for right now? How about running backs? Flowers had a career-high 101 yards after the catch in Week 7. He now leads all wide receivers in YAC this year. He's played several games without Lamar Jackson. So what do we project Flowers to look like once Jackson returns and with more reps in this Declan Doyle offensive system that fits his skill set perfectly? That projects like a league winner. Other early Week 8 waiver wire targetsMason Taylor, TE, Jets: The Jets showed signs of wanting to get Taylor more involved last week and he played a major slew of snaps in Week 6. He followed that up in Week 7 with 62 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions. Geno Smith looks for him in the red zone and his blocking keeps him as a near full-time player. For that, he's worth scooping up in deeper leagues that start multiple tight ends.Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins: Talent has never been an issue for Douglas, who has flashed elite releases off the line of scrimmage, stop-and-start ability to create separation, and breakaway speed prior to this week's game. Unfortunately, all of those moments came in training camp. Finally, the upside was actualized in Week 7 when Douglas racked up a long touchdown, 70 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Devin Singletary, RB, Giants: Singletary executed a perfect jump cut to make the safety miss in the hole and create a game-winning touchdown run for the Giants in Week 7 but that's not why he makes this column. Despite the Giants entering a bye week, Singletary is a sneaky add after Tyrone Tracy Jr. left Week 7 in the first half with a lower-body injury. Cam Skattebo also left in overtime with a hamstring injury he considers minor. It's possible neither Skattebo or Tracy are out when the Giants return from the bye, but just in case, you might want to stash Singletary. Eli Raridon, TE, Patriots: Raridon was a Beyond The Boxscore favorite due to his intriguing tape at the collegiate level, and those traits have shown up in bunches during his rookie season so far. Raridon caught another touchdown in Week 7 and also racked up 56 yards.Tez Johnson, WR, Buccaneers: Johnson and Baker Mayfield built a rapport last season that was glaring and obvious when you watched the Buccaneers. He's a sleeper to keep an eye on and an early lookahead stash.

Hardy hasn't played in 2026 while recovering gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason

        Eli Drinkwitz gave Missouri fans some great news on Sunday evening. Star running back Ahmad Hardy will return to practice this week after recovering from a gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason, the school announced Sunday.Back in May, Hardy was shot in the upper leg while attending a concert in Mississippi. He was taken to the hospital for emergency surgery, and he hasn't seen the field at all this season due to his recovery.Earlier this season, Drinkwitz was asked about Hardy's progress, and he promised that he would announced when the star running back returned to practice."I really don't want to have to answer that question every week, and I will tell y'all when there is an update," Drinkwitz said. "... There's no update. He hasn't began a two-week ramp-up period. If he practices, I promise I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete. We'll just do it ourselves."
Drinkwitz made good on his promise Sunday, although Hardy's status for Saturday's game against Arkansas is still unknown.
Hardy was arguably the best running back in the country last season as he led all Power Four player with 1,649 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns.With Hardy out due to his rehab, Jamal Roberts has filled in nicely for the Tigers. Roberts ranks seventh in the country with 867 rushing yards, and his eight rushing touchdowns are tied for 18th. If Missouri can get Hardy back to anything resembling the player he was last season, it will have the best running back tandem in the nation.
The Tigers may be able to let Hardy ramp up this week, but they have to be eyeing a return for a November home stretch that includes Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Missouri's offense will need as much help as it can get against those defenses.

title: Bermuda Championship pushed to rare Monday playoff after only 54 holes - CBS Sports
description: Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power will return to Port Royal tied for the lead, with a U.S. Open spot and locked-
body:
Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power will return to Port Royal tied for the lead, with a U.S. Open spot and locked-in PGA Tour status on the line
        
        
                                                                                                            
                                                    By
                                                
                                                            STATS
                                                    
                    
                                    
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        SOUTHAMPTON, Bermuda (AP) -- Raging wind at Port Royal caused unplayable conditions that led to cancellation of the final round Sunday at the Bermuda Championship. Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power were to return Monday morning for a sudden-death playoff.Gusts topped 40 mph (65 kph) in the morning, and none of the 72 players who made the cut was able to start the final round. Officials decided a few hours later to cancel play on Sunday, and with a forecast just as dire, made it a 54-hole tournament.Smotherman and Power were tied for the 54-hole lead, and the plan was for them to return at 9 a.m. local time (8 a.m. EDT) for the playoff at the par-3 16th hole, weather permitting.
The most recent Monday finish on the PGA Tour was at the Travelers Championship in June, when Viktor Hovland defeated Scottie Scheffler. The last time a PGA Tour event was reduced to 54 holes was the 2024 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am, which ended on a Saturday.Smotherman and Power are entered in the Mexico Open next week in Vallarta, Mexico, and a charter plane was due to take other players in the field.
Power is just outside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup Fall, and a victory would not only lock up his card through 2028 but put him in the elite Championship Series in the new 2028 schedule. Smotherman won his first PGA Tour title in Utah earlier this month. Another victory would earn him a spot in the U.S. Open.

title: Real Madrid finally show their potential under Jose Mourinho in convincing El Clasico win over Barca - CBS Sports
description: Kylian Mbappe scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid in a 2-1 win at Barcelona on Sunday, trimming the gap between
body:
Kylian Mbappe scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid in a 2-1 win at Barcelona on Sunday, trimming the gap between the rivals to three points
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There is an air of inevitability when a player is in peak form, to the point that their teams develop a very entertaining type of dependence on them. At the team's best, the player is merely the focal point in a harmonious system; otherwise, that player is almost resigned to the reality that they exist in large part to bail their team out of trouble. Barcelona felt like the best-case scenario before El Clasico after both Lamine Yamal and Raphinha got off to strong starts to their seasons, Tuesday's 4-2 loss at Paris Saint-Germain doing little to dampen their spirits. If anything, it was Real Madrid who have become overly reliant on Kylian Mbappe over the years, Sunday's game slated to be no exception.Over the course of Real Madrid's 2-1 win at the Camp Nou, though, the roles had reversed.Mbappe and Raphina were each on the scoresheet, neither feat much of a surprise considering each of their exploits this season. Early in his third season with the club, Mbappe notched his 99th and 100th Real Madrid goals on Sunday while Raphina registered his 13th goal in nine LaLiga games this campaign. Both showcased the inherent ability of a dependable superstar, each of them providing a unique snapshot of the teams they represent.The France World Cup winner was the finishing piece of a team whose defensive efforts won them the game, neutralizing a Barcelona team that had won nine games out of nine to start the domestic campaign. The visitors opted to cede play to the possession-oriented hosts, holding the ball just 37.6% of the time in the process. Los Blancos also let the attack-minded Barcelona roll out Plan A, outshooting the visitors 18 to 10 along the way. Jose Mourinho's side were fully prepared for the challenge, their positional discipline designed to ensure their opponents would be unable to do much with all of their efforts. Hansi Flick's side registered just 1.19 expected goals from all their attempts, well below their average tally of 3.5 expected goals per game in LaLiga this campaign.
Yamal and Raphinha, as well as winger Anthony Gordon, had the ball at their feet on multiple occasions and looked certain to go for goal. They were often restricted to taking shots from sundial positions, Real Madrid's defensive shape holding nicely for much of the game. In the moments the Barcelona players' individual brilliance came through, a Real Madrid defender would find a way to shut things down before it was too late. Aurelien Tchouameni led the charge at the base of Los Blancos' midfield, excellent as the visitors resisted Barcelona's press and prevented them from racking up opportunities in moments of transition. He was hardly alone – Federico Valverde excelled at right back, while Marc Cucurella came in clutch on the flip side. Even Arda Guler and Yan Diomande maintained their standing in their wide attacking positions, limiting Barcelona's ability to create much despite racking up touches and passes.It allowed Mbappe to pounce when the ball finally landed, even if he was less visible over the course of the 90 minutes than usual. He took just 36 touches and three shots, down from his average in LaLiga this season of 52.7 touches and 5.2 shots per game, but he is the exact type of player to survive a game state like this one. His first was a gift from Barcelona's back line while his second was a team effort, one that showcased his own brilliance as much as it did Eduardo Camavinga's abilities off the bench in maintaining Los Blancos' structure before notching the game-winning assist.
Mbappe exploited a Barcelona back line that had tried to turn over a new defensive leaf this season, perhaps haunted by the mistakes their aggressive high line has made since Flick took the job two years ago. Rodri, whose Golden Ball award goes hand-in-hand with Spain's World Cup win this year, is as well-positioned as any to be a one-man solution but he was unable to fix Sunday's problems by himself. The injuries to Barcelona's defense have not helped, another coming midway through the first half when left back Xavi Espart came off for Alejandro Balde, but Mbappe was not alone in getting the better of the hosts' back line. Jude Bellingham had his moments, while Guler played a key role in the build-up to Mbappe's first goal.
In the process, Real Madrid closed the gap atop LaLiga to three points and rebooted a title race that many were ready to call two months into the season. Unlike the 2023-24 team that picked up the team's last major title, they found a way to win on Sunday not on the back of excellent individuals who are living, breathing cheat codes. For the first time since Xabi Alonso's surprise dismissal in January, they notched a convincing win on the back of a strong game plan and an even more impressive ability to execute it.

body:
Be careful touting signature wins too early during college football season.Paper champions loading up on early victories can easily be extinguished by midseason when inflated schedules come to a grinding halt during conference play. We've seen it happen across the SEC, Big Ten and now Big 12, following the league's wildest weekend yet.There's the flip side too -- teams can get hot and find their footing after the opening month, strengthening an opponent's resume thanks to a prior result.The current AP Top 25 rankings give us a snapshot of which wins have aged well and which are depreciating assets ahead of the first College Football Playoff poll on Nov. 3. Beating a top-10 team in September that later disappears from the rankings doesn't preserve a ranked victory on that résumé. With the postseason picture taking shape, it's time to revisit some of the memorable results from earlier this fall. 
These are the squads who banked something meaningful and those in search of more approaching the final month of the campaign.Wins that aged wellNo. 12 Alabama 45, Kentucky 17When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Kentucky's current ranking: No. 9The Crimson Tide handled the SEC's current leader its only loss this season by four touchdowns and did so despite multiple first-half turnovers and a halftime deficit. Alabama outscored Kentucky 32-0 in the second half, and guess what? The Wildcats haven't lost since. That's one of the most insane rebounds in SEC history for a first-year coaching staff. The victory was Alabama's ninth straight over Kentucky and marks the Crimson Tide's lone win over a team currently ranked in the top 25.No. 4 Texas 24, No. 1 Ohio State 23When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Ohio State's current ranking: No. 2If Texas finds itself in the middle of the SEC's nine-win pack a few weeks from now, the Longhorns will have something others do not -- one of the best nonconference victories of the season. Everyone knew that the 20-point comeback win over Ohio State would carry significant weight, and the Buckeyes are one of only two unbeaten teams in Big Ten play.
The Buckeyes' season could torpedo from here without Julian Sayin given what's left on the schedule, but that's not the expectation. Ohio State is confident in its quarterback room behind Sayin and has a Heisman candidate who can bail this offense out of difficult spots when the ball's thrown in his direction.No. 13 Texas Tech 28, No. 22 Houston 26When: Sept. 18 (Week 3)Houston's current ranking: No. 18Cougars coach Willie Fritz put it succinctly after his team's narrow loss in Lubbock in mid-September, where a failed two-point conversion in the final moments proved the difference. "There's no moral victories," Fritz said after losing to Texas Tech last month. "We came here to win. And we didn't win."
Houston's 4-1 since that setback after its four-game winning streak was snapped Saturday night at Utah. This remains Texas Tech's only ranked win, with another opportunity coming in Week 9 against Arizona.No. 5 Miami 33, Wake Forest 20When: Sept. 19 (Week 3)Wake Forest's current ranking: No. 14The Demon Deacons are arguably the ACC's second-best team on the heels of four consecutive wins entering next weekend's home game against Virginia. Their only loss in league play is to the Hurricanes, and they've outscored their last three opponents, 132-24, in the ACC. Jake Dickert is getting the most out of UNC transfer quarterback Gio Lopez (17 touchdowns, one interception) and Wake Forest controls its own destiny in the race for a spot in the ACC Championship Game.Miami's Darian Mensah completed an ACC-record 24 straight passes in this victory as the Hurricanes jumped out to a 31-7 lead midway through the third quarter behind his brilliance and early success with Malachi Toney. Miami dominated this road matchup for three quarters, but the final score doesn't reflect how one-sided it really was.
No. 4 Notre Dame 41, Wisconsin 13When: Sept. 6 (Week 1)Wisconsin's current ranking: No. 25No one knew if the Badgers would recover after flatlining at Lambeau Field against the Fighting Irish during Labor Day weekend, but Wisconsin did show some unexpected fight in that one for 2.5 quarters to open a pivotal campaign for Luke Fickell. Wisconsin's only loss since was last week's 17-7 setback at UCLA, as Saturday night's win over 16th-ranked USC pushed the Badgers to 5-2 overall.No. 12 Kentucky 35, No. 18 LSU 34When: Oct. 10 (Week 6)LSU's current ranking: No. 15The second of consecutive overtime wins for Will Stein and the Wildcats this season, Kenny Minchey called his own number on the game-winning quarterback draw, sending Kroger Field into a frenzy. LSU is unbeaten since, with consecutive blowout wins against SEC opponents, to pull back inside the top-15. These are two of four SEC playoff picks in our latest bowl projections, and there's a chance each finishes with 10 wins. Who would've predicted that for the boys in blue three months ago?No. 15 BYU 28, Arizona 17When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Arizona's current ranking: No. 20In the Big 12 opener for both teams, the Cougars erased a 17-14 halftime deficit, scoring a pair of touchdowns after intermission to prevail as the only defense to quiet the Wildcats up to this point. Arizona improved to 6-1 overall after Saturday's victory over Iowa State and is now ranked. Quarterback Noah Fifita has given opposing defenses problems the last four seasons and gets a chance to cause chaos with upcoming contests against Texas Tech and Utah down the stretch. BYU would love for Arizona to play spoiler and make its road to the playoff that much clearer.
Wins that aged poorlyKentucky 31, No. 9 Texas A&M 21When: Sept. 19 (Week 3)Texas A&M's current ranking: NRDozens of Kentucky fans were in my mentions this week asking why the Wildcats weren't included in our group of five teams with at least two ranked wins this season. That's because their team's demolition of the Aggies at Kyle Field was the beginning of the end for Texas A&M's place in the top 25. The Aggies, now 4-4 overall,  were our most overrated team in the preseason top-10 and proved that quickly this fall after replacing several starters in the trenches and having no answer for the loss of KC Concepcion at wideout. Kentucky simply exposed glaring issues before anyone else could.No. 7 Alabama 56, No. 16 Mississippi State 23When: Oct. 3 (Week 5)Mississippi State's current ranking: NRHanding Kamario Taylor and the Bulldogs their first loss of the season was a memorable road beatdown in Starkville, but Mississippi State hasn't won a game since and has tumbled outside of the national rankings. The Bulldogs were shut out by LSU, struggled at home in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma and now travel to Texas on Halloween. Keelon Russell's four total touchdowns in this game pushed him toward the front of the Heisman race before those hopes evaporated after losses to Georgia and Tennessee.Michigan 17, No. 11 Oklahoma 10When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Oklahoma's current ranking: NRSo much for the Wolverines using their promising start under Kyle Whittingham. They've moved on from Bryce Underwood as their starting quarterback. Then, Tommy Carr's first career start resulted in a six-point dud during Saturday's overtime loss to Indiana. Michigan's defense remains this team's calling card, but the Wolverines are not scoring enough points to keep pace in the Big Ten or CFP races.
No. 9 Ole Miss 41, No. 24 Louisville 38When: Sept. 6 (Week 1)Louisville's current ranking: NRLouisville was believed to be a title contender this season in the ACC considering Jeff Brohm had registered 29 total wins his first three years with the Cardinals, but a 4-3 start has left much to be desired in the middle of the conference. Consecutive losses to Wake Forest and NC State eliminated Louisville from legitimate league title hopes and exposed the real issue for this team - they can't stop anyone. Ranked in the lower third of the ACC in total, scoring and pass defense, the Cardinals can blame themselves for this rapid deterioration. Heading into Week 8, the only countable ranked wins for Ole Miss were LSU and Missouri.Northwestern 34, Penn State 13When: Oct. 2 (Week 5)Penn State's current ranking: NRDon't tell any Northwestern folks this win lacked significance. At the time, the first game at the new $875 million Ryan Field was a memorable one after the Wildcats galloped their way to 413 yards rushing, but the Nittany Lions have completely flatlined since. Winless in the Big Ten after four games, this was Matt Campbell's second crack at a conference opponent after losing at home to Wisconsin the previous week. Northwestern's now ranked and 6-1 overall after Saturday's win over Rutgers, but the next three games will ultimately determine this team's value against Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State.Colorado 14, Georgia Tech 13When: Sept. 3 (Week 1)Georgia Tech's current ranking: NRDoes anyone still remember this one? Both of these teams stink and will need strong second halves of the campaign just to get bowl-eligible. Deion Sanders and the Buffaloes have lost five straight following Saturday night's 57-24 beatdown from Oklahoma State, while the Yellow Jackets are 1-5 this season against Power Four competition, the lone victory coming against Duke on Oct. 10.
Virginia 34, NC State 8When: Aug. 29 (Week 0)NC State's current ranking: NRAn opening-weekend game many thought would determine part of the top-end ACC standings turned out to be pretty much meaningless. Virginia lost at home to Duke on Friday night, falling to 4-4 on the year, hours before NC State's loss at Stanford marked the end of Dave Doeren's tenure as leader of the program. The second Power Four vacancy this cycle, the Wolfpack will have a search for the first time in 14 years after moving on from the ACC's second longest-tenured coach.

title: NFL overreactions: Panthers' loss raises Bryce Young concerns, Ravens in danger - CBS Sports
description: There had been few more encouraging starts to the season than the Carolina Panthers. Even though they were only 3-2 through six weeks, t
body:
There had been few more encouraging starts to the season than the Carolina Panthers. Even though they were only 3-2 through six weeks, the Panthers' offense was humming, and Bryce Young had taken a huge step forward. Combine that with a faltering NFC South, and it looked like the Panthers were already on their way to a second straight division title.And then came this week. Buccaneers 43, Panthers, an emphatic reminder that things are rarely what they seem in the NFL. And that Week 6 is way too early to even pencil in anything as far as the playoffs go. With that, we get to overreactions and reality checks. Carolina got the latter served, cold, on Sunday.The Panthers had the most disappointing, worst loss of the NFL seasonOverreaction or reality: RealityThere is simply no other way to state it. This was one of the most stunning displays -- or lack thereof -- we've seen in the NFL of late. Add in the opportunity that the Panthers had at home, plus everything else this game represents, and it's a truly awful Sunday from Carolina.Bryce Young threw two interceptions and got sacked five times, one of which resulted in a Calijah Kancey scoop and score. Remember all those terrible outings from the first two years of his career where he looked completely overwhelmed from a physical perspective? This looked very much like that.
Young was truly awful in every aspect. His pocket escapability wasn't up to par, and Todd Bowles overwhelmed -- there's that word again -- him throughout the afternoon.But really, the Buccaneers overwhelmed the Panthers in every aspect. Carolina had one carry of 15+ yards ... and it was by backup quarterback Kenny Pickett in garbage time. Young didn't get much help from anyone up front; the Buccaneers registered 13 pressures and had six quick pressures (2.5 seconds or faster). That might get worse, too: Right tackle Taylor Moton suffered a fractured fibula, got carted off and is out indefinitely.The defense might have been even worse. The Buccaneers ran for 258 yards -- their fourth-most ever -- and three touchdowns. Oh, and we can't leave out special teams, where the Panthers had a blocked extra point returned for two points and a muffed punt. Find a way a team can get embarrassed, and the Buccaneers did it to their division rival.
Every team has bad weeks, but this was more worrisome in the big picture. Young and the offense have now had a middling week and a bad week since their Week 5 bye. The offensive line has given up the most pressures and the most quick pressures in the NFL. The defensive line now ranks dead last in yards per carry allowed (5.2) and is dealing with significant injuries to both of its cornerbacks.The Panthers have been brought back to Earth, and they've brought the rest of the division back into things. With a chance to separate from the pack, the Panthers still lead the NFC South at 3-3 but are just a half-game up on the 3-4 Falcons, with the 2-5 Buccaneers and 2-5 Saints also still in a not-very-inspiring division race.Dan Campbell's fourth-down decision was reasonableOverreaction or reality: RealityThe Lions beat the Packers 20-17 Sunday despite a horrific failed fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line late in the fourth quarter.
Lots of people were probably pulling their hair out saying "What is Dan Campbell thinking?!"Well, he explained what he was thinking: "Well, I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. And those were the two thoughts."Here's why it's defensible. To his first thought, the Lions were two-for-three on fourth-and-1 this season and are 10-for-14 since the start of last season.
But when they didn't get it, his second thought came into play. The Lions had all three timeouts with nearly five minutes remaining. The Lions would have almost certainly gotten the ball back with significant time/timeouts left, no matter what happened. In fact, the short field for the Packers basically worked in the Lions' favor.Would you rather have him punt the ball away and give the Packers the ball with five minutes and 40-50 yards to go to reach field-goal range? There's a solid chance the Packers score with basically no time left and/or the Lions use up all their timeouts in that scenario.Would I have gone for it there? Probably not. But Campbell's logic is legitimate here, and analytical models supported it or had it as a toss-up.
It ended up working out, too. The Packers had to settle for a field goal attempt, which was blocked, and the Lions drove down and won on a walk-off field goal. But even if Trey Smack's kick had gone in, the Lions would have had the ball with 3:21 left and all three timeouts, only down three. Campbell would take that every day of the week.Don't think "Oh, there's dumb Dan Campbell making a dumb, over-aggressive decision." It was defensible at worst and completely reasonable -- and maybe even the right choice -- at best. And guess what? His team won!The Vikings should regret trading J.J. McCarthyOverreaction or reality: OverreactionIn arguably the best performance of his young career, J.J. McCarthy threw for 252 yards in a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He made some truly exquisite throws and didn't have a single turnover, an issue that had plagued him with the Vikings. Meanwhile, the Vikings slugged out a 16-10 win over the Colts. Minnesota is 6-0, but the offense continues to be stop-and-start to put it nicely.
To not put it nicely -- and, frankly, more accurately -- it has been bad. Minnesota's 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions. Only the Chargers score a touchdown on a lower percentage of their drives this season. Only Cam Ward and Daniel Jones have a lower touchdown rate than Kyler Murray this season. That's bad company. The traditional run game has been poor, and while Murray has had some big plays, but down-in and down-out, it's been very poor.
But 1) it's been one game for McCarthy, so let's not go overboard, and 2) it just wasn't working out in Minnesota for him. It wasn't. He was bad in training camp. He was bad in the preseason. He was bad and/or hurt last season.Sometimes players need a change of scenery. Sam Darnold needed many. And, again, it's too early to deem McCarthy a success story in New York. Vikings fans can want a better offense and realize it wasn't going to happen with McCarthy.
The Ravens will miss the playoffsOverreaction or reality: OverreactionFor the first time since 1996, the Ravens have blown a double-digit halftime lead. This week, they led the Bengals 13-0 at halftime before losing 35-13.Yes, that's a 35-0 second half for Cincinnati, the team's best and most important half in a long, long time. The Bengals are 4-2 and, after looking completely asleep in the first half, they looked like a Super Bowl-caliber outfit in the second half.Baltimore was once again without Lamar Jackson, though he's expected back next week. His return can't come soon enough. The Ravens are now 4-3, which is fine, but they're 0-2 in the AFC North. Their offense looks like one of the best in the NFL with him and one of the worst without him. Add in that the defense has struggled in crucial situations -- 29th in yards per play allowed and just one sack in second halves this year -- and you get a team that has limited margin for error.
Jackson and the Ravens will face the Bills next week and then the Jaguars. They need to win one of those two -- at least -- to get back on track, and then an easier stretch (Chargers, at Panthers, Texans, Buccaneers) ensues. I'd bet on Baltimore figuring it out with Jackson back.The 49ers can't win a Super Bowl with their current offenseOverreaction or reality: RealityChristian McCaffrey was the latest 49ers weapon to get hurt, though at least he returned in San Francisco's eventual 29-20 loss to the Falcons. It's the 49ers' first loss of the season, and given their offensive personnel, it's amazing it took this long.Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel both missed the game. De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson remain on IR. Ricky Pearsall is out for the year.
The 49ers had four active wide receivers Sunday: Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Christian Kirk (in his first game of the season after a calf injury). More than half of Purdy's completions went to George Kittle or McCaffrey.Everything fell apart last week when Evans exited, and with a short week, the 49ers didn't have any answers. How could they? This isn't an injury bug at wide receiver. It's injury Godzilla.The good news is the bye is here, and reinforcements should be coming back. If they don't -- or if they get hurt again -- the 49ers will be looking at more offensive issues.The Saints should fire Kellen MooreOverreaction or reality: OverreactionLess than two weeks ago, Saints owner Gayle Benson called the Saints' 1-4 start "not acceptable" and called out coach Kellen Moore and GM Mickey Loomis by name."Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution."Then, last week, Benson showed up at Friday's practice, hugged Moore, and endorsed him, per ESPN, saying no change is imminent. Talk about a seesaw. The Saints beating the Giants helped.But then the Saints lost to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris this week. Will Benson go back to seemingly putting Moore on the hot seat?She shouldn't. This is a team still emerging from a years-long long run of misguided win-now moves after Drew Brees retired. Tyler Shough has shown positive growth under Moore, and the NFC South is eminently winnable. First-round pick Jordyn Tyson is getting closer to returning. The defense has been banged up. A 2-5 record is unsightly, but Moore deserves at least through the end of this year -- and I would argue a third season next year -- before New Orleans makes a decision to move on.It's Fernando Mendoza time for the RaidersOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe Raiders lost to the Rams 35-21, Las Vegas' fourth straight loss after a 3-0 start.Does that mean Fernando Mendoza time? No. Kirk Cousins played well -- again -- in this game with 295 passing yards, two touchdowns and zero turnovers. The Raiders are giving him no help in the running game: Mike Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty combine for 42 yards on 14 carries, which is already a bad number before you realize half of those yards came on one carry.Listen, even when the Raiders were 3-0, I was saying they wouldn't make the playoffs. But the Raiders are *only* 3-4, and they play the Jets next week. Benching Cousins would send the wrong message to the team. If they were 2-5 or worse, or if Cousins were struggling, then Mendoza time would be closer. But not right now.That doesn't mean it won't happen at some point. Let's say the Raiders win next week to get to 4-4. You can't bench Cousins then. But then comes a tough stretch of at 49ers, Seahawks, at Broncos, at Browns. Then comes the bye week. I think Mendoza will take over at some point mid-November, or perhaps at the Week 6 bye. But now would be far too early for all parties involved.Bo Nix had a breakthrough that will carry overOverreaction or reality: Part overreaction, part realityBo Nix threw for 222 yards on 7.7 yards per attempt in Sunday's win over the Cardinals -- both his best numbers since Week 2. Those numbers lie, somewhat, though. Nix's 52-yard touchdown pass was ... you guessed it ... a screen.
But there was legitimate progress in downfield aggressiveness. Nix's 11.1 air yards per attempt were a season high, and his four completions of 20+ yards were his most since Week 2. And perhaps most importantly? Nix looked to create. Going from one big play where he didn't do much (above) to a big play where he did a lot ...
Seeing Nix move and look to make plays is huge! He had a 27.3% scramble rate in 2024 and a 16.1% scramble rate last year. This year, it's down to 7%. Maybe it's the ankle fracture and surgery from last season that's still in the back of his mind. But this is an important step -- or however many steps it took him to cover 62 yards.Long story short, there were moments of breakthrough: the running, the aggressive throwing, the pressure mitigation. There were moments of non-breakthrough: barely over half his passes were completed, too much inconsistency. The Cardinals' defense must be factored in, too. But this was a half-step in the right direction.

        Welcome to the Week 7 grades!We have somehow hit the final Sunday of October, and when you look at the NFL standings, there are definitely a few surprises. For one, the Cleveland Browns are in first place in their division. I repeat, the Cleveland Browns are in first place. This is not a drill. One reason the Browns' magical run is happening is because of Deshaun Watson. During Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee, Watson engineered another fourth-quarter game-winning drive on Sunday, and he now has five on the season. That makes him just the third QB since 1970 to have a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season. Not to be outdone, the New York Giants are also in first place of the NFC East, AND they just won a game with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback. If I had told you in August that the first-place Giants were going to win a Week 7 game with J.J. McCarthy under center, I would have been laughed at on the internet. No one's laughing now. The Giants have now won a game with three different starting quarterbacks this year (McCarthy, Jameis Winston and Jaxson Dart). That makes them the first team since the 2016 Patriots to win at least three games with three different starters before November. On the other side of the standings, the Baltimore Ravens are in last place after suffering one of the most shocking losses in NFL history. The Ravens led the Bengals 13-0 at halftime but ultimately lost 35-13. That's the third-largest loss in NFL history by a team that led by at least 13 points at halftime. Since 2020, the Ravens have lost 17 games in which they led by double digits at some point, the most in the NFL in that span. All three of their losses this year have come in games where they held a double-digit lead. This was the second straight week where they shut out their opponent in the first half, only to go scoreless and lose in the second half. To make matters worse for the Ravens, the two teams we mentioned earlier -- the Giants and Browns -- are coached by two people the Ravens got rid at the end of last season (John Harbaugh and Todd Monken).

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When J.J. McCarthy got traded from the Vikings to the Giants, he called it "a shock" but also "an opportunity to take advantage of."When Cam Skattebo received zero touches in Week 6 -- one week after a costly fumble -- he admitted he wasn't expecting the lack of involvement, but it also forced him "to kind of step back and look at it and figure out why."Every NFL player faces pivotal moments -- make-or-break situations where they must dig deep and find a way to respond. Both challenges and opportunities in one. These were McCarthy's and Skattebo's. And in their biggest moments thus far in their young careers, they made their stand."I think that's exactly the story," John Harbaugh said about his team responding. "I mean to that's the point. It tells you who they are. You might have thought before the game 'We're gonna find out about our guys. We're gonna find out about who they are.' And we did."
In his first start with New York, McCarthy threw for 252 yards and had no turnovers, and in his return to prominence in the lineup, Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a touchdown as the Giants upset the Texans 27-21 in overtime. Skattebo's 42-yard rumble -- the longest run of his career -- set up Devin Singletary's walkoff score.
Before the overtime bursts, though, McCarthy put on a laser show against one of the NFL's most talented defenses. He smartly leaned on Malik Nabers (seven catches, 111 yards), who is looking very much like he's back to pre-ACL tear form, and made several truly outstanding throws.
McCarthy completed five throws of at least 15 yards downfield after completing six last week as a sub. The 11 completions are his most in a two-game span in his career ... and he didn't even sub in for Jameis Winston until the fourth quarter last week.
This is what the Vikings had hoped McCarthy would be when they drafted him: an athletic quarterback with a live arm able to access every part of the field. For McCarthy to do this, given the circumstances -- traded just weeks earlier, making his first start on the road against a really good defense -- was shockingly impressive."It's that thing: It's guys have scars," Harbaugh said. "He has scars. He's been wounded. He's been wounded. He's been battered. But you heal stronger, and you become better because of it, so you should be grateful." Skattebo, meanwhile, ran over, around and through Houston's defense. His 7.3 yards per carry represented the best of his career, and he credited the offensive line for opening up holes; his 65 yards before contact were the most in any game in his career. He also told the team's postgame show that he had ball security on his mind, which wasn't the case against Washington.
The common denominator between McCarthy's and Skattebo's performances? Harbaugh, the man who gave both players opportunities: Skattebo an opportunity to learn, McCarthy an opportunity, period.The end of Harbaugh's time in Baltimore was defined by disappointment. After 18 years and a Super Bowl triumph with the Ravens, Harbaugh watched a Tyler Loop field goal sail wide in Week 18 last year, ending Baltimore's playoff hopes. He never got Lamar Jackson and co. over the hump. His reputation took a major hit in turn.But perhaps it took too big of a hit. This coach has won 184 games. He won double-digit games 11 times in 18 years in Baltimore. That included his first year, when he turned a 5-11 team from 2007 to an 11-5 team in 2008. He knows how to build a winner and sustain a winner.
The early returns are that he's doing it again in New York. The Giants are 4-2-1, two wins ahead of anyone else in the NFC East. The Giants have won with Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston and, now, McCarthy as starting quarterback. They're the first team since the 2016 Patriots to have three different winning starting quarterbacks within the first seven games of the year.And this one meant as much as any regular-season win has. Just look at how Harbaugh reacted:
"I'm having a lot of fun," Harbaugh said, a smile coming to his face. "I'm having a lot of fun. There was a little dancing in the locker room."
McCarthy used that "fun" word, too."It was a lot of fun. So much fun to be out there playing football, but with this group, it makes it that much more fun, that's for sure."And that's what these Giants were Sunday: fun. Fun to see McCarthy shining in a spot no one could have envisioned him in just a few weeks ago, when he was sitting on the Vikings' bench. Fun to see Skattebo ripping off big gains and Nabers making wild catches. Fun to see Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux wreaking havoc.Fun to see that, after losing their quarterback in Week 2, they're still playing well and still winning. Everything could have gone off course after Dart's injury. Instead, the Giants will head into their bye with their heads held high, in first place in their division and with meaningful football ahead.
"It's a reward," Harbaugh said. "Now you've got to make something of it. It doesn't mean anything if you don't build on it, right? Well, it means something, but it doesn't mean we're gonna win a championship yet. It means we have an opportunity."... We're gonna be in this thing until the end."

schema.headline: John Harbaugh's Giants improve to 4-2-1 as J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo star in OT - CBS Sports

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers reveals NFL once had a completely different plan for its international games - CBS Sports
description: Rodgers is now the first quarterback to play an international game in three different countries in three straight
body:
Rodgers is now the first quarterback to play an international game in three different countries in three straight years
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No quarterback is as well-traveled, at least when it comes to football, as Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The four-time MVP is the first quarterback in NFL history to play an international game in three different countries in three straight seasons. He played in London, England, in 2024; Dublin, Ireland, in 2025; and Paris, France, in 2026. After Rodgers' Steelers won 16-10 in the NFL's first game in Paris, the quarterback revealed that when the NFL and the NFL Players Association were negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement in 2020, they almost had a different plan for international games. The NFL and its players' union were in talks to hold an international week in which the 16 games for its 32 teams would take place in 16 different locations around the world. With all games outside of the United States that week, the season would be 16 games long, and each team would have two bye weeks. Rodgers said those conversations died when owners pushed for a 17th regular-season game, which did come to fruition in 2021. "The reach of the league is fantastic, and I think I always wanted to be a part of it," Rodgers said postgame. "I think it'd have been phenomenal for the game. Now, the owners wanted to push for 17 games for the extra revenue because they care so much about player safety, but it would have been nice."Where could the NFL have played 16 international games? Rodgers sees multiple opportunities in North America, South America, Europe and even the Middle East. The only barrier he saw to the league making a groundbreaking effort to expand its global reach is money. 
"I think there are great opportunities for expansion in those things," Rodgers said. "It'd be awesome to see them, you know, have an international week because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game. And I wish there was a mandate, though, from the league [that] they would have to open up their pocketbooks too, and they're maybe a little tight on money and stuff. I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. You could do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work. But they won't because they're tight [with money]."The 22-season NFL veteran didn't go abroad in his first 17 seasons with the Green Bay Packers, but he finally experienced the chance to play internationally for the first time in London in his final season with the Packers in 2022. After three straight years playing a game overseas with the New York Jets and the Steelers, Rodgers couldn't be a bigger proponent of the NFL's international initiatives. 
"You know, I said it earlier this week: 'I wish we could have come over and enjoyed the sights both in Ireland and in France for a little more time,'" Rodgers said postgame, via Front Office Sports.  "But it's great the way the game is growing."

        Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has scored his first touchdown as a member of the Houston Texans, doing so in Week 7 against the New York Giants. He made it to the end zone in his second game with the team, after being traded on Oct. 11 from the Arizona Cardinals. The former No. 4 overall pick caught the pass from a QB he has caught numerous touchdowns from: His former college quarterback, C.J. Stroud. Watching the two connect for a TD was a blast from Ohio State past.Here's a look at the big play:
The 6-yard touchdown came as the first half was winding down and, paired with the ensuing two-point conversion, tied the game at 14 all. The touchdown was his first reception of the game.
Harrison caught one touchdown for the Cardinals in four games, a TD that also just so happened to be against the Giants. He is the first player to score a touchdown against the Giants with two different teams in the same season since Herschel Walker did it in 1989 as a member of the Dallas Cowboys and Minnesota Vikings.In four games with the Cardinals, Harrison had five receptions on 13 targets for one touchdown. Last week, in his Houston debut, he had three receptions on four targets for 34 yards. 
The Texans are currently 2-4 and on a two-game winning streak as they look to turn their season around.

McCaffrey expressed his frustrations with his limitations during the game

        The San Francisco 49ers are perfect no more, falling to the Atlanta Falcons, who were 2-4 going into the contest. While the Niners lost, they can breathe a sigh of relief that they don't seem to have lost their star running back, who went down for a short time with a thigh injury. Christian McCaffrey appeared to aggravate his leg in the first quarter, then went to the medical tent and eventually to the locker room in the second quarter. He was initially listed as questionable, but he returned to start the third quarter. Losing McCaffrey for any amount of time significantly impacts the offense, considering he is consistently the team's leading rusher.After the game, the four-time Pro Bowler gave an update and explained what happened with his leg."I have no idea. It sucks, because I feel like I was going on a run there, and my leg just died on me," CMC said. "I was trying to get it going for the whole rest of the game, but it just sucks trying to play like that."
He added some reassurance on his health, saying, "I know I'll be alright, but it's just really frustrating."McCaffrey had a diminished workload when he returned to the field. Before going down with the injury, he had four carries for 29 yards and one touchdown. His first rushing attempt back from the locker room was a loss of two, and he finished the game with seven carries for 39 yards and one touchdown. He also finished with six receptions for 61 yards, clocking three receptions for 45 yards before the injury.His 39 rushing yards are his second-fewest this season, while his 61 receiving yards are his best in 2026. For someone whose job uses their legs the most, having their legs feel like they "died" doesn't seem positive, but the RB didn't seem concerned about the long term. 
The 30-year-old has a long history of injuries, and any sign of him not looking 100 percent will give his fanbase flashbacks, and not the good kind. The Niners have suffered numerous significant injuries this season and cannot afford to lose any more star players.The 49ers have a bye coming up, which could work in McCaffrey's favor. Whether this injury will linger beyond Sunday will be known once the weekly injury reports come out.In Week 7, the 49ers offense was without wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (IR), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (IR). The running back room includes rookie Kaelon Black and second-year RB Jordan James. McCaffrey leads the team in carries and rushing yards this season, with Black behind him and their QB third on the list.
